newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 19.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- Irish police on Tuesday delivered a bodyblow to IRA terrorist plans when vital bomb components were seized and a number of people arrested.
- The Irish government and the Olympic Council of Ireland (OCI) clashed again on Tuesday night, seven months after the Atlanta controversy over Sonia O'Sullivan deeply divided Irish sport.
- A high court ruling on reporting restrictions could set an appalling precedent, a leading law lecturer said on Tuesday night.
- Almost 50,000 Irish Permanent mortgage and savings account holders have been given a September deadline to claim more than 14 million free shares worth 86 million Irish pounds.
- Sterling plunged five pfennings against the German mark on Tuesday as currency speculators took profits and the last faint hopes of an early rise in UK interest rates faded away.
- Five people are in custody after Irish police uncovered an IRA bomb-making operation near Portlaw, County Waterford, and disrupted a major arms supply route into Northern Ireland.
- Sean O'Callaghan, the former IRA terrorist turned police agent, is to appear in a United States court to testify against an ex-IRA prisoner fighting deportation proceedings.
- One of the oldest signs of a human settlement discovered in Ireland has been dug out of the mud flats in the Shannon Estuary.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton on Tuesday expressed surprise at remarks by the Northern Ireland Secretary in which he rejected calls for an apology for the deaths on Bloody Sunday in Londonderry.
- The government-run Bord Gas will spend 26 million Irish pounds in a new drive to help sign up another 50,000 homes.
